_README: Provenance for the committed baseline CSVs that had no record: the ten ranking exports in
data/baseline/rankings/ and the trade-value chart in data/baseline/trade_value/.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Audit section 7.10 found provenance coverage INVERTED: the four
secondary market sources each carry an ATTRIBUTION.md, and the two Sleeper projection CSVs
carry sleeper_projection_provenance.json -- while the PRIMARY valuation input, the
highest-weighted source in the composite (COMPOSITE_SOURCE_WEIGHTS 1.3) and the one feeding
CDME's bpa, was documented nowhere but prose in README.md. The input questioned least was
documented last.
WHY THE ORIGINATING VENDOR IS NOT NAMED HERE, AND WHY THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT.
The rule this file was written under: state the origin of information wherever the origin is
not pay-locked; where it IS pay-locked, describe the file honestly and leave the vendor
unnamed. These eleven files are derived from a PAID SUBSCRIPTION EXPORT that the repository
owner obtained under that subscription's own terms. Writing the vendor into a provenance
record is not a neutral act of documentation -- it asserts a posture about what may be
retained and redistributed from a subscription product, and that assertion belongs to the
owner, not to this file.
This is deliberately NOT the same act as README.md naming the vendor. README describes the
app's workflow to its own user -- 'upload your export here' -- which requires the name and
makes no claim about redistribution. A provenance record travels with the committed data.
Do not 'fix' the omission by copying the name across from README; the two are different
statements. If the licensing posture is ever settled explicitly, this note is the place to
record that decision, and only then does the name belong here.
EXPECTED LIFESPAN. The stated intent is to rework the input set toward publicly-sourced data,
at which point the constraint above dissolves and these records can name their origins
outright. Section 19.11.2 (the committed baseline goes permanently Stale at +90d with no
refresh path) is folded into that same rework, not solved separately.
WHAT IS RECORDED INSTEAD. Everything that is a fact about the file itself: scope, shape, the
date the source carried, how it got here, and what reads it. Those are the facts a reader
needs to judge whether a number is trustworthy, and none of them is pay-locked.
THIS IS DOCUMENTATION, NOT AN INPUT. Nothing reads this file at runtime.

_common.origin: paid subscription export, vendor deliberately unnamed -- see _README
ingest_method: Exported from the vendor's own tool by the repository owner, then parsed to CSV by the
vendor-specific PDF/CSV parser family in data_merger.py (grep that module for its parse_
functions; they are named after the vendor, which is why the name is not transcribed
here), and committed as the offline pool DataMerger reads when no upload is present.
_common.source_date_field: the date the export itself carried, not the date it was committed here
known_limitations: Section 7.9/#78: two of the PDF parsers joined stats to names by positional index with no
verification. Repaired (#82, #83), but rows ingested before that repair are the reason a
row's numbers should be treated as vendor-reported rather than vendor-verified.
Section 19.11.2: these files carry a fixed source_date and have no refresh path short of a
new export, so the freshness grade degrades monotonically from the dates below.

_note: Ten format-scoped ranking exports covering the SAME player pool under DIFFERENT league
settings -- that is the point of carrying ten rather than one: rank and trade_value are
format-dependent quantities, and DataMerger selects the file matching the active format.
The two sleeper_*_projections.csv files in this directory are NOT covered here; they have
No projection or proj_3yr column: the IDP export carries a RANK, not a point
projection. That absence is the supply defect #51 measured -- 0 of 415 IDP rows are
projected, and the draft exhausts IDP supply at rounds 14-15 as a result. The '.corrected'
suffix marks a hand-repaired parse, which is itself why these rows are the ones to
re-derive first when the input set is reworked.

superflex_idp_rankings.corrected.csv._note: Same shape and same caveat as ppr_idp_rankings.corrected.csv.

_note: The only committed source that prices PICKS as well as players, which is why it is loaded
separately (data_merger.load_all(..., default_kind='trade_value_chart')) rather than as an
eleventh rankings file: its rows carry asset_type/value and no rank, and #85 settled that
the flat future-pick price here is the distribution's centre rather than a placeholder.
